We've now probed the empty, invalid, and large-collection edges across every part of the app, and each is settled. Before I propose building the real thing, one assumption I want to make explicit rather than silently bake in:

- **Your bookmarks are saved and stay there between visits.** Everything you save — links, tags, notes, their to-read/done/archived state — should still be there when you close the browser and come back later. (In the prototype the list resets on reload; only your sort/page-size preference persists. In the real app the bookmarks themselves would persist too.) Is that the expectation — a private store that's just yours and endures?

Here's where we've landed. **So far these flows are settled:**

1. **Quick saving** — paste a link, its title and description are fetched for you and are editable; add your own tags and a "why I saved it" note. Save even when a page can't be reached; incomplete links are flagged gently; pasting a link you already saved opens it for editing instead of duplicating.
2. **Three ways to hold a link** — *To read*, *Done*, and *Archived*, where archiving is separate from reading status and restoring returns a link to exactly where it was. Plus editing and permanent deletion.
3. **Finding things** — per-view search across title, link, description and note (case-insensitive), with a precise query language (`#tags`, `"exact phrases"`, `and`/`or`/`not`, parentheses) and click-a-tag filtering.
4. **Handling a big collection** — sort by date added or title, choose 10/25/50 per page, move through in groups, with your sort and page-size remembered.

One thing I've **set aside for later**: showing each site's real favicon and preview image (right now it's a coloured letter) — a visual polish item, not a change to how anything works.

**May I now start building this scope as the real application?** (I'll switch from exploring to implementing only once you say yes.)
